title: Capital Small Finance Bank Ltd - 544120 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.
summary.overview: Gross advances reached INR 9,074 crore, up 22% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while deposits grew 16% YoY to INR 10,596 crore with CASA at 36.7%. NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

financial_highlights.change: from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 and 4.06% in Q1 FY26
GNPA -28 bps YoY, -7 bps QoQ; NNPA from 1.39% YoY and 1.24% QoQ
broadly in line with last year

segments.name: Business loans (MSME and other)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 27% of book (22% a year ago) and 35% of incremental disbursements; MSME grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ, with average ticket INR 28 lakh and yield on business loans at 10.5%.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Stable at 25% of book (around 26% a year ago); grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY, with housing yield at 9.87% vs 9.85% in Q4 FY26; average housing ticket INR 20-25 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Share fell to about 27% from 30% a year ago; target ticket INR 5-35 lakh (average INR 30 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters and 50% LTV collateral.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Stable at 14% of book; calibrated lending to well-rated corporates.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: Yield of 12.27%; grew 5% QoQ and 18% YoY.

segments.name: Consumption loans
segments.commentary: Stable at around 7% of book, mostly top-up loans; 2-3% of the book is loan against deposits or securities.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Advances outside Punjab grew over 30% YoY and are 25% of the book (24% in Q4 FY26, 21% a year ago).

guidance_outlook: FY27 advance growth guided at 22%; FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crore plus.
NIM expected to hold around 4.2% through FY27, with expansion in FY28 and FY29 as average CD ratio rises from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s.
ROA targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE targeted at 15% plus by FY29.
Medium-term net NPA target of around 1% (below 1% per Vision 2029); management expects stable PCR from here.
Opex to see some improvement in FY27 (currently 2.95-2.98% of assets) after Q1 salary increments; larger opex growth expected in FY29.
Around INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27, with a 10-12 bps benefit that management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories as of June 2026; 74% of branches are semi-urban and rural.

Average CD ratio at 83% (vs 80.9% in Q1 FY26); management targets mid-to-high 80s, implying an incremental 3-6% from deployment of investments and interbank balances (yielding about 7-7.5%) into advances at about 10.5-11%.
Liquidity coverage ratio averaged 184.18%; capital adequacy at 21.6%.
demand_pricing: Competition in housing loans from PSU banks has eased due to deposit repricing, with mortgage growth recovering to 10% YoY; housing yields held at about 9.87%.
Private universal banks focus above INR 1 crore tickets, leaving the INR 10-50 lakh MSME band to the bank; management says it prices slightly above market for service and turnaround time.
Agri yields are priced 25-35 bps above PSB rates for INR 5-25 lakh tickets; management cites industry-wide risk premium rather than bank-specific pricing.
Cost of deposits fell to 5.6%; the spread target of cost of deposits vs advance yield is 5.05-5.3%. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1% a year ago.
Management said 50% of advances are fixed-rate and 50% floating-rate; 48.67% of the book resets annually, mainly MCLR-linked; MCLR was raised by 10 bps in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Split of MSME growth between Punjab and Haryana, and how it is trending
qa_highlights.answer: MSME (INR 28 lakh average ticket, middle-income, collateralised) grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ; growth within Punjab and outside Punjab, and between Punjab and Haryana, is similar. Advances outside Punjab are 25% of the book vs 24% a quarter ago and 21% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable
qa_highlights.answer: PCR was raised to 54.5% to move net NPA towards the medium-term 1% target; management says most of that action is done and it expects a stable PCR from here.

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining repricing is not material; the bulk was done in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27. ROA is targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6%+ by FY29; Q1 ROA was 1.3% vs 1.18%, and PPOP margin rose to 2.04% from 1.94%.

qa_highlights.question: What keeps NIM stable at around 4.2% given cost-of-deposit and yield pressure
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27 for a 10-12 bps benefit, which management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%; 50% of the book is fixed and 50% floating; NIM expansion is expected in FY28-29 as average CD ratio (83%) rises to mid-to-high 80s.

qa_highlights.question: Why PSU competition in housing eased and whether mortgage growth will pick up
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit repricing helped the bank compete with PSBs in the INR 20-25 lakh housing ticket; mortgage grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY at a 9.87% yield vs 9.85% in Q4, but management says growth will stay moderate with some portion still to be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Agri yield levels and risk mitigation
qa_highlights.answer: Agri average ticket is INR 30 lakh (range INR 5-35 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters, priced 25-35 bps over PSB rates in the INR 5-25 lakh band; collateral LTV is 50%, and management attributes the premium to industry-wide risk perception.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 repricing of about INR 1,597 crore of term deposits: the 10-12 bps benefit is expected to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs, so NIM holding at about 4.2% depends on this.
Advance yield has fallen to 10.9% from 11.1%, and the business loan yield is 10.5%; further yield compression would pressure the 5.05-5.3% spread target.
SMA-2 rose to 3.11% from 2.71% in the quarter, though total SMA-1 and SMA-2 fell to 4.78% from 5.47% a year ago; management called the rise not meaningful.
Opex at 2.95-2.98% of assets; management expects a moderate FY27 increase, with larger opex growth in FY29, which could weigh on the ROA path.
Average CD ratio of 83% needs to reach mid-to-high 80s; management says advance growth will outpace deposit growth in Q2 and Q4, and deposit growth is strongest in Q1 and Q3.
Universal bank conversion depends on getting net NPA to about 1%, which the bank currently reports at 1.14%.
key_quotes: We expect NIM to stabilize at the current levels for the FY27 and start further expanding, supported by improving CD ratio i n the coming years.
So, our advance should outpace our deposit growth for some peers, maybe 2 years or so, which is the one factor which we are taking care.
Now we think a majority of that action has been done.
We are not taking advantage of that and believe that particular benefit will be taken away /off setted by the increasing cost of deposit.
summary.management_tone: Confident and specific on growth, asset quality and the ROA trajectory, with the NIM and yield outlook framed as stable rather than expanding in FY27. Management was more cautious on housing growth, which it said is still recovering, and on how much cost-of-deposit repricing is left.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed 22% FY27 advance growth, backed by 16% deposit growth, 83% average CD ratio, MSME growth of 49% YoY and a 216-branch network, with no specific new capacity or order book quantified.
